1.w: And Agrippa was saying to Paul, “It is permitted you to speak for yourself.” Then Paul, having stretched out the hand, began his defense:

2.w: “Concerning all of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I esteem myself fortunate before you, being about to defend myself today,

3.w: you being especially acquainted with all the customs and also controversies of the Jews. Therefore I implore [you] to hear me patiently.

4.w: Then indeed my manner of life, which [is] from youth, having been from [its] beginning among my nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews know—

5.w: knowing me from the first, if they would be willing to testify—that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived [as] a Pharisee.

6.w: And now I stand, being judged for the hope of the promise having been made by God to our fathers,

7.w: to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, serving in earnestness night and day, the hope concerning which I am accused by the Jews, O king.

8.w: Why is it judged incredible by you⁺ if God raises the dead?

9.w: Therefore I indeed in myself thought [it] to be necessary to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth,

10.w: which I also did in Jerusalem. And I also locked up many of the saints in prisons, having received the authority from the chief priests; and [on] their being put to death, I cast against [them] a vote.

11.w: And in all the synagogues, punishing them often, I was compelling [them] to blaspheme. And being exceedingly furious against them, I was persecuting [them] even as far as to foreign cities,

12.w: during which, going to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,

13.w: at midday on the road I saw, O king, a light from heaven above the brightness of the sun having shone around me and those going with me.

14.w: And all of us having fallen down to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me? [It is] hard for you to kick against the goads.’

15.w: Then I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

16.w: But rise up and stand on your feet. For I have appeared to you for this, to appoint you as a servant and a witness both of that which you have seen of Me and of the things in which I will appear to you,

17.w: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you

18.w: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, [that] they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those having been sanctified by faith in Me.’

19.w: Hence, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

20.w: but also first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, also to all the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, I was declaring to repent and to turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

21.w: On account of these things the Jews, having seized me (being in the temple), were attempting to kill [me].

22.w: Therefore, having obtained help from God up to this day, I have stood bearing witness both to small and to great, saying nothing other than that which both the prophets and Moses said was about to happen:

23.w: that the Christ would suffer [and], as first through resurrection from the dead, He is about to proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles.”

24.w: Now of him making this defense, Festus said in a loud voice, “You are insane, Paul! Much learning turns you to insanity!”

25.w: But Paul says, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus, but I declare forth words of truth and sobriety.

26.w: For the king understands concerning these things, to whom also I speak, being bold. For I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him, for this thing is not done in a corner.

27.w: Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe.”

28.w: Then Agrippa [said] to Paul, “In so little [time] do you persuade me to become a Christian?”

29.w: And Paul [said], “I would wish anyhow to God, both in a little and in much, not only you, but also all those hearing me this day, to become such as I also am, except these chains.”

30.w: Then the king and the governor rose up, and Bernice and those sitting with them,

31.w: and having withdrawn, they began speaking to one another, saying, “This man is doing nothing worthy of death or of chains.”

32.w: Then Agrippa was saying to Festus, “This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
